title: Japan national CPI (January 2027), 08:30 JST
source: EST: stat.go.jp/english/data/cpi/1582.html ('Consumer Price Index — Schedule of Release', page's own 'Last Update : 23 January 2026'), re-fetched raw direct 2026-09-05 (HTTP 200, 13,839 bytes) and parsed cell-by-cell out of its single 17-row HTML table by this session. Against the header 'Japan: Survey month | Date of release || Ku-area of Tokyo (preliminary): Survey month | Date of release || Remarks', the second-to-last row parses exactly as ['January, 2027', 'February 19', 'February', 'February 26', ''] — i.e. the January-2027 national CPI releases 2027-02-19, with the Tokyo February flash following 2027-02-26. The empty Remarks cell is itself evidence: this release carries no yearly or fiscal-yearly average. 2027-02-19 is a Friday and is clear of Japanese public holidays per the Cabinet Office's own list (www8.cao.go.jp/chosei/shukujitsu/syukujitsu.csv, HTTP 200, 21,538 bytes, Shift-JIS, fetched by this session the same day; the nearest 2027 holidays are 2027-02-11 and 2027-02-23). Filed estimate on three counts, identical to its sibling rows: the confirmed-prefix taxonomy has BLS:/BEA:/CENSUS: for US statistical agencies and no slot for Japan's Statistics Bureau, this lane may not self-confirm an event it discovered in-sweep, and the schedule page's own last-update stamp is 2026-01-23. The 08:30 JST release time is the Statistics Bureau's standing convention and is NOT read off this page — treat it as the weaker half of this entry
notes: DISCOVERED during the japan-cpi-2027-03-19 initial-research adjacency sweep (2026-09-05), and the reason it is tracked: this is the LAST NATIONAL CPI READING THE BANK OF JAPAN HOLDS when it decides on 2027-03-18 (boj-decision-2027-03-18, estimate). That matters because it is the number that measures how much the March MPM's one-day miss of the February print (japan-cpi-2027-03-19, estimate) actually costs. The japan-cpi-2027-03-19 ledger benchmarked it: across 27 Februaries (2000-2026, e-Stat 2025-base files parsed locally), the national January core y/y sits 0.178pp mean absolute and 0.116pp median from the national February core y/y it precedes, against a Bureau that publishes to one decimal — so on the median February this print rounds to the one the board 'misses'. The same benchmark found that the Tokyo February flash (japan-cpi-tokyo-flash-2027-02-26, estimate), released a week after this print, beats it as an estimate of national February core in only 9 of those 27 years. That is the finding: THIS print, not the flash, is the better free estimate of the print the BoJ does not get. Impact is LOW for the same reason every Japanese CPI entry on this calendar is: no house playbook is keyed to Japanese prices, symbols is empty, and the value here is corridor structure and calibration rather than a price channel. Nothing tracked on this calendar sat anywhere in February 2027 before this entry.
